_meta.description: Every question about Scripture Alone: price, languages, Mac, Apple Watch and Android, translations and imports, privacy, share links and availability.
can-i-add-another-translation.4b1e7a: Can I add another translation myself?
can-it-help-me.3f2cf8: Can it help me find verses for what I'm going through?
does-it-work-on.d22ae5: Does it work on Apple Watch?
everything-people-ask-about.83f908: Everything people ask about Scripture Alone, from what it costs (nothing) to where its translations come from.
how-do-share-links.af837c: How do share links work? Is my verse sent anywhere?
is-scripture-alone-available.8b64bc: Is Scripture Alone available in the European Union?
is-scripture-alone-in.a326a4: Is Scripture Alone in my language?
it-s-a-careful.2cd1ba: It's a careful, word-for-word translation in the public domain, so it can be given away freely — the Berean Standard Bible and King James Version are included for the same reason. Translations like the CSB, ESV, NKJV and NASB need publisher licenses, which we're requesting.
no-google-play-download.8a9d61: No Google Play? Download the APK from GitHub, with every translation and study tool built in. It doesn't update itself, and it can't be updated by the Google Play version, so read the notes there first.
none-there-are-no.762c80: None. There are no analytics, no trackers and no accounts. Your highlights and notes stay on your devices and sync only through your own private iCloud, which I can't see.
scripture-alone-is-in.15e523: Scripture Alone is in English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Italian. Each language comes with a whole Bible of its own — the 和合本, the 文語訳, the Lutherbibel 1912, Louis Segond, the Reina-Valera 1909, the 개역한글, the Bíblia Livre and the Riveduta — with its own book names, verse numbers and typed references. The commentary and lexicon definitions exist only in English.
the-link-carries-the.8f367c: The link carries the verse itself, after the “#” in the address. Browsers never send that part to a server, so this site never sees what you shared: the page rebuilds the card right in the browser. If Scripture Alone is installed, the link opens the passage in the app instead.
the-word-and-nothing.59b9cc: The Word, and nothing in the way.
to-join-join-the.9646c8: To join, join the beta group, then opt in on Google Play with the same Google account and install it from there. If Google Play says the test isn't available yet, the first build is still in Google's review, so try again in a day or two.
until-they-can-be.7d3638: Until they can be included in the app, two files are known to import well. For the ESV, the ePub edition of the Reformation Study Bible. For the CSB, the pew Bible PDF its publisher offers. Open either with Import a File… in Translations.
where-can-i-get.11aafd: Where can I get the ESV or the CSB to import?
yes-in-a-closed.b8b573: Yes, in a closed beta on Google Play: a native app for Android phones and tablets, with its own Wear OS app. Your highlights and notes stay on the device, since there's no iCloud on Android.
yes-no-ads-no.bf78fd: Yes. No ads, no in-app purchases, no subscriptions. Scripture Alone is free, and it will stay free.
yes-on-any-mac.d853c7: Yes, on any Mac with Apple silicon. Install the iPad app from the App Store on your Mac, and your highlights and notes sync with your iPhone and iPad through iCloud.
yes-open-go-to.b8d503: Yes. Open Go To and choose a topic, or tap See All for the whole directory: 72 themes such as anxiety, grief, loneliness, fear, doubt, guilt, temptation, illness, marriage, parenting and money worries, each with the passages that speak to it, shown in whichever translation you read. You can also just type what you're feeling, like “worried” or “lonely”, into search, and the matching topic appears above the verses. The themes are in all nine of the app's languages, and English readers can also browse Nave's Topical Bible, over five thousand topics from A to Z.
yes-scripture-alone-can.230191: Yes. Scripture Alone can open a USFM file, a DRM-free ePub or a Bible PDF you own, and it can fetch the free catalogue published by eBible.org when you ask it to, with your own language first — nothing is downloaded unless you tap. What you import is yours alone: it follows you to your other devices through your own private iCloud, and copying and sharing from it follow the publisher’s own published terms. This is an interim arrangement: requests to license the major modern translations are with their publishers, and if those are granted the translations will simply be in the app, and this may go away.
yes-scripture-alone-is.9112b8: Yes. Scripture Alone is on the App Store everywhere in the European Union, France included. The source code is open to everyone on GitHub.
yes-the-full-source.c48195: Yes. The full source is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license.
yes-the-watch-app.14dc16: Yes. The watch app carries its own copies of the American Standard Version, the Berean Standard Bible and the King James Version, so it reads offline even without your iPhone nearby, and it follows the translation you're reading on your iPhone — including one you imported. It has the Verse of the Day, your favorites and notes, can read a passage aloud, and puts the day's reference on your watch face.
